title: Claude Code: Auto Mode, Concise Style & the August 2026 Update
content:
## Overview

August 2026 brought Claude Code's biggest permission-model change since its launch, plus a new default output style and a design-in-the-terminal skill. This page covers what shipped and why it matters for day-to-day use.

---

## Auto Mode Becomes the Default

On **August 14, 2026**, auto mode became the default permission mode for new Claude Code sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans. Instead of asking for approval before most tool calls, the agent now proceeds on its own — unless the action it wants to take is judged **irreversible, destructive, or aimed outside your local environment** (e.g., pushing to a remote, sending a message, deleting files).

Two controls matter more than the default itself:

- **Prompt-injection screening** on incoming content (file contents, web pages, tool output), to catch attempts to redirect the agent's behavior before they reach the model.
- **Hard deny rules** you configure yourself, so specific actions can never be taken regardless of what the model concludes mid-task.

### Allow/Deny Rules as Plain Sentences

Rules are no longer just glob patterns like `Bash(git *)`. Auto mode supports **`hard_deny`** and **`soft_deny`** rules written as plain English sentences (e.g., "never force-push to main"), which live in **user-level settings** so project-level settings cannot silently override them:

- **`hard_deny`** — blocks the action unconditionally, no override possible.
- **`soft_deny`** — blocks the action unless a direct in-session request or an explicit allow rule overrides it.

Deny rules and explicit "always ask" rules hold in *every* permission mode — they're the levers to configure regardless of whether a given session starts in auto mode or the older prompt-per-action mode.

---

## Concise Output Style

Shipped in **v2.1.237**, the new **Concise** output style makes Claude lead with the result and skip the preamble and step-by-step narration Claude Code normally gives, while doing the same depth of engineering work behind the scenes. Enable it via `/config` → Output style → Concise, or by setting `"outputStyle": "Concise"` directly in a settings file. Like other output styles, a change takes effect on the next `/clear` or new session, since it's baked into the system prompt at session start.

---

## /design Skill

A new `/design` skill turns an idea or a screenshot into an editable interface directly from the terminal — generating a working UI mockup without leaving the CLI session.

---

## Session & Workflow Improvements

- **Auto-continue after usage limits** — a session now automatically resumes once a usage limit resets, instead of requiring the user to manually restart it.
- **Extended weekly limits** — the 50% increase to weekly usage limits (Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans) was extended through **August 31, 2026**.
- **GitLab merge request support** in the worktree view (v2.1.233).
- **Memory limits on build commands**, to prevent a runaway build from exhausting session resources.
- **Stronger credential-leak protections** bundled with the auto-continue release.
- Broader platform support: new **Bedrock** and **Alpine** support, plus a **Python 1.x upgrade helper** for projects migrating major Python versions.
- Improved `/resume` and `/goal` behavior, and smoother fullscreen, proxy, and messaging handling in cloud sessions and remote control.

---

## Why It Matters

Auto mode is the clearest signal yet that Anthropic is optimizing Claude Code for long, mostly-unattended runs — the same trend behind scheduled tasks and remote sessions (see *Claude Code Overview*). The tradeoff is real: less per-action confirmation means the deny-rule configuration (hard_deny/soft_deny) is no longer optional hardening, it's the primary safety mechanism for anyone running sessions unattended.
